{"self_assessment": "Impact: I made the early start possible by fetching a full load of 40 dominoes for the shared bin at the very beginning. The bin stayed stocked for the whole activity, and nobody else needed to make a supply run. I also stood a domino back up at the nose split, which helped the fall pass into both body lines. I then carried the top line's tail on into the upper flare, so the top fin was part of what fell. The final picture reads clearly as a fish, with a nose on the left, two body curves and a flared tail.

Execution: I chose the batched fetch because it costs far less per domino than small trips. I extended the top line's tail in several short stretches, and I inspected the nose, the tail and the flare join repeatedly, so the table knew what was connected. When the flare join needed work, I cleared the patch and then left it to the people already working there. That kept the crowded spot from getting more cluttered before the push.

Collaboration: I backed the fish idea at once and kept the team informed throughout, saying where I was working and which line I was taking. I offered to close the join when needed and said when I was staying hands-off. I kept the mood light and positive during a tense final few minutes.

Leadership: I committed to the plan early and took on the practical supply job so the builders could stay on the lines. I called out the nose split problem and the tail-end gap as I saw them. In the last minutes I kept everyone clear of the finished picture before the push. I'd put my share of the result at roughly a fifth, concentrated in the supply, the nose fix and the top tail.", "my_share_percent": 22}
